definitions.explanation: The V-shaped fabric or leather strap on traditional Japanese footwear such as geta (wooden clogs) and zori (flat sandals) that passes between the big toe and second toe to hold the foot in place.

examples.japanese: {鼻緒|はなお}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{切|き}れた→切れる：01936_kireru⟧。
⟦{赤|あか}い→赤い：00585_akai⟧{鼻緒|はなお}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{下駄|げた}→下駄：03984_geta⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{買|か}った→買う：00489_kau⟧。
examples.english: I bought a pair of geta with red thong straps.

examples.japanese: {鼻緒|はなお}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{足|あし}→足：00575_ashi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{当|あ}たって→当たる：01860_ataru⟧⟦{痛|いた}い→痛い：01108_itai⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で、⟦{新|あたら}しい→新しい：00506_atarashii⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{替|か}えたい→替える：13399_kaeru⟧。
examples.english: The thong strap rubs against my foot and hurts, so I want to replace it with a new one.

notes:
USAGE:
{鼻緒|はなお} refers specifically to the strap found on traditional Japanese sandals (⟦{草履|ぞうり}→草履：04048_zouri⟧, ⟦{下駄|げた}→下駄：03984_geta⟧). The strap passes between the toes and is often made of fabric.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {鼻緒|はなお}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{切|き}れる→切れる：01936_kireru⟧ (the strap breaks)
- {鼻緒|はなお}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧すげる (to attach/replace a thong strap)
- {鼻緒|はなお}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧ゆるい (the strap is loose)

CULTURAL NOTE:
A broken {鼻緒|はなお} was traditionally considered a bad omen in Japanese culture, particularly when leaving home.
